walkthroughs.body_html:
Commercial Production — a core area of Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Commercial Production brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Commercial Production.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: They glow when touched.

mcqs.q: What property do shape memory alloys have?
options: They glow when touched.
They return to a pre-set shape when heated.
Current stays the same.
They remember every shape they have ever been bent into.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CAD and CAM?
options: CAD creates digital designs; CAM uses those designs to control manufacturing machines.
They are the same thing with different names.
They glow when touched.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.

sequence.def: Commercial production starts from a frozen design
Processes are matched to material, volume and cost

sequence.term: Design and make tooling and jigs
sequence.def: Dedicated equipment is produced and proved
A trial run validates quality and cycle times
Volume manufacture starts after the pilot passes
Ongoing checks keep output within specification
